originality.rationale: The inspected 2026 bundled-modalities case study axiomatizes the operator without a labelled finite-frame count or a growing-agent probability law. KR 2021 gives general non-normality examples. Pittel 2000 gives the discrete-meet event, which is strictly weaker than the exact per-world singleton-agent coverage event, and its fixed-agent theorem does not determine the growing-agent threshold. The already established two-agent comparison case does not imply the three-agent or growing-agent conclusions. No equivalent or broader published implication was found among the materials actually inspected. Residual priority risk from inaccessible 2023 full text and possible classical coverage enumerations is disclosed.

value.rationale: The count L_{n,r} is the natural complete census of finite S5 frames where a fundamental group-knowledge operation becomes an ordinary S5 modality, including meaningful multi-agent cases not subsumed by pointwise comparability.
